newsitem.title: japan: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - March 18.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Tuesday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- The Finance Ministry plans to tighten rules on financial holding companies, particularly those established by banks and insurance firms.

-- Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) plans to build an undersea optical-fiber cable network linking the United States, China and Japan by 2000, in cooperation with Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co, China's Posts and Telecommunications Ministry and AT & T Corp.
-- The site of a fire at the Tokaimura nuclear reprocessing plant was not reinforced to withstand fire and explosion.
-- Outstanding debt at Japan Highway Public Corp will likely swell to 35 trillion yen in 2013.
-- Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto eyes earlier target for finance reform plan.
-- North Korean defector Hwang Jang Yop will leave Beijing today for the Philippines en route to Seoul.
-- The government is likely to approve on March 28 a bill on the revision of a law on the forced lease of land in Okinawa.
